leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B045 prize to Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov, with citations that differ only in wording (physiology of GLP-1 and its active form enabling incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity). What is shared is the three names, the single-part structure and the view that the prize rests on the physiology and peptide discovery, with the drugs as evidence of significance. What is not shared is the weight given to Knudsen's drug-design contribution: El-Manira opened with Knudsen and moved to the Mojsov trio, and several members state that excluding her has a real cost. Members also differ on the fallback: four name B003 and B015 as alternatives, one names B003 and B006, one names B003 and B025.

areas_of_agreement: B045 is the only ballot in the six round-1 configurations, and all six prefer the identical laureate trio.
Maturity is not in doubt for B045: the mechanism is confirmed by large independent outcome trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes.
The discovery chain runs from proglucagon processing and incretin physiology (Holst, Drucker), through the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), to therapies.
Unanimity in the opening is not accepted by any member as a merit argument in itself; each rests the case on the science.
A single-part B045 prize avoids the arbitrary exclusions that a six-name optogenetics ballot (B006) or a two-part configuration would impose under the three-person cap.
B003 appears as the first-named alternative for all six members.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should reward the physiology and peptide discovery alone, or also the translation into long-acting agonists, and how the citation should express this. All six raise it, and none treats it as resolved.
Whether the commercial scale of semaglutide and tirzepatide distorts how original the underlying science appears (raised by El-Manira and Svenningsson).

Whether optogenetics (B006) counts as a discovery in the physiological sense. El-Manira says yes, and Sandberg (as reported by El-Manira) discounts it as mainly a research tool with limited clinical impact so far. The B006 position is explicit only in El-Manira's configuration.
How much weight the unfolded protein response (B015) should carry given its disease relevance is still developing. El-Manira ranked it lower on that ground, while four members list it as a fallback.
Long-term safety and durability of GLP-1 therapies are still being studied (Wahren-Herlenius).
attribution_disputes: Four names are credited on B045 and three seats exist. All six configurations drop Knudsen, and all six flag that exclusion as a risk of reading the prize as stopping short of the therapy.

Mojsov's priority for the active peptide form is described as contested, and Habener, who is not among the credited names, is part of that dispute. No member claims to have resolved this from the supplied evidence, and several say priority details are recalled and not verified against primary sources.

El-Manira and Perlmann treat the third seat as a choice between crediting peptide identification (Mojsov) and crediting drug design (Knudsen). Both treat Knudsen's work as a real mechanistic contribution, not merely industrial.

For B003, members cite the Zhou issue and Frazer's priority relative to parallel VLP groups as a residual attribution concern, and zur Hausen's prior prize covers the viral aetiology and not the vaccine.
For B006, which three of six credited names best reflect the discovery and neuronal demonstration is unresolved (El-Manira).
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B045.
For B003, the question is not maturity but how much the prior zur Hausen recognition and the Zhou and Frazer priority questions should count against it as a competitive alternative.
For B015, the stated reservation is that its disease relevance is still developing, not doubt about the discovery.
For B025 (named by Linnarsson) and B006 (named by El-Manira), the round-1 files give no explicit maturity argument.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Perlmann and Svenningsson both disclose about twenty co-authored works together (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy); both state no connection to any shortlisted candidate and no recusal.
El-Manira and Perlmann each disclose co-authorship with each other (a 2009 paper, and one work respectively); neither person is credited on a shortlisted ballot.
Sandberg and Linnarsson disclose mutual co-authorship (and Sandberg with Jonas Frisén); none is connected to a shortlisted candidate.
Svenningsson discloses a past Rockefeller link to Paul Greengard, who is not a candidate.
El-Manira notes work in motor-circuit neuroscience where optogenetics is widely used, with no documented tie to any B006 candidate.
No member reports a conflict or recusal tied to any credited name on a shortlisted ballot.
questions_for_round2: For the third B045 seat, does the committee credit Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) or Knudsen (acylated long-acting analogues), and what evidence on Mojsov's priority relative to Habener is available in the supplied materials?

Does the committee want to reward GLP-1 physiology and discovery alone, or also the translation into therapy, and how should the citation be worded so that Knudsen's role is acknowledged if she is not a laureate?
If B045 cannot be settled on attribution, which single alternative is the committee's first fallback, B003, B015, B025 or B006, and on what grounds?
Is a two-part prize with B045 reduced to two names worth considering, as Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius raise it, or does the committee keep the single-part B045 prize with three names?
Can the HPV priority questions (Frazer, Zhou and parallel VLP groups) be settled well enough to make B003 competitive, and how much does zur Hausen's earlier prize count?

Which of the six B006 names, if any, would the committee credit for the discovery and neuronal demonstration, and does the member who ranks B006 fifth or lower still object to its research-tool character?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete agreement on one ballot, B045, and the same three names, with all of the remaining disagreement concentrated in the third seat, the Mojsov priority question and the discovery-versus-translation framing. Fallback preferences are more scattered than the lead position, so round 2 should test B003 against B015, B025 and B006 only if the B045 attribution cannot be settled.
